en: The elder brother, Master Sanfo, was like the Double Peaks where one slips their feet; his bathing water boiled with fervor, and his wisdom-light shone brilliantly.
He accepted with a willing heart the malice and anger of the wicked, wearing ten layers of the armor of patience. They could not bite through him, as hard as iron or sour paste;

he swallowed the "thorny burr" whole. At Xixi, jade was struck; at the pond, gold was pounded. Now, these remaining writings are entrusted to the pear and jujube trees: when the dawn breaks at midnight, the sun shall be red.
Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Daoning of Kai Fu Bao Ci Chan Monastery in Tanzhou, respectfully inscribed by Mi Shan Jing of the former Mahāyāna school.
Composed by Tan Zhang, a retired Court Gentleman for the Propagation of Righteousness (Xuanyi Lang), of Zhao Shan.
The transmission of the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Eye reached the thirty-third generation at Caoxi with Huairang.
Huairang received Mazu, after which it became the Linji school. After six transmissions, Ciming truly revitalized it.
Ciming’s disciples were Yangqi Hui, Huanglong Nan, and Cuoyan Zhen; all were known as "lion cubs" who could let out a roar that pacified the region.
Fubo (Subduer of the Hundred Beasts) succeeded Baiyun Wenzhun; Wenzhun succeeded Wuzu Fayan. When Fayan sat upon Mount Dongshan, he was known as "The Great Fulfillment.
Later in life, his character became solitary and austere, granting his seal of approval to few; those who inherited his dharma were two Qins—one Qinruo and one Qinyuan—and Ning.

The Master was Ning. He was quick-witted and possessed steadfast devotion; he traveled extensively to consult masters in all quarters, receiving their seals of approval and trusting in the conditions of his karmic affinity.

During the Daoguan era, while serving as the First Seat at Tianning Monastery in Huxiang, he was selected by Governor Xi Gong—who held the rank of Waitaizhi—to lead Kaifu Monastery, whereupon he entered the world of public teaching.
Zen disciples gathered in great numbers, with the assembly exceeding five hundred; those who came were like those with copper heads and iron faces.

When he encountered [obstacles], they were shattered to pieces; though possessed of a clever mouth and eloquent tongue, upon arrival, he was as if mute. With a single staff, he severed the tangled vines of past and present;
with a single whisk, he pointed out the barriers of the great thousandfold world-system. Walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—there was nothing that was not his wondrous function.
Speaking or remaining silent, moving or still—all were acts of Buddha-work. Although he had been in this world for but a short time, his benefit to others was vast. Thus, his testament states:
The *Ji-ge* (Verses on Quiescence) states: "Having resided in this monastery for five years, I have perceived them all as lasting but a moment.
Thus, it is not an error to say that forty-nine years were not spent in vain. The disciple Shanguo compiled these words and phrases; I have here recorded their general outline.
Tanzhou: It is now requested that Dao-ning, the head seat (shouzuo) of Chongning Chan Monastery in Chengxia, proceed to Kaifu to serve as the abbot (changlao),
open the hall for the sake of the state, and expound the Dharma to offer prayers for the longevity of the Emperor.
Regarding the Venerable Master’s longevity:

I humbly submit that the lightning flash and the spark from a flint can hardly catch up with the subtle mechanism of his smile; the meditation board and the sitting mat have already revealed the meaning of his wordless intent.
Although "mind itself is Buddha" and from the beginning there has never been a single thing, yet without speaking and without demonstrating, there would be no means to realize emptiness;
one must rely upon a person to open up this profound principle. Master Ning is an elder whose numinous roots were planted in former lives and whose ancestral lineage has transmitted its fragrance.
He has opened wide the gate of non-duality and aspires to transform the great chiliocosm. Regarding the matters pertaining to his school’s tradition, all deliberations have reached a consensus.
I return. It is fitting that you follow the request to restrain your ambition and specifically attend this long-vacant seat. The clay ox and wooden horse shall enter the sea and neigh in the wind;
the lame tortoise and blind turtle shall avoid drowning and instead strike against the wood. I respectfully submit this note.
On the [blank] day of the second month in the third year of the Daguan era,
the Memorial was composed by Xi Zhen, Court Petitioner, formerly Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Huigyou Pavilion,
currently serving as Governor of Tanzhou and Military Commander of the Jinghu Nan Road Pacification and Commandery.
The Recorded Sayings of the Nineteenth Abbot, Master Ning, of Kai Fu Chan Monastery in Tanzhou, Capital District; Imperial Uncle, Commander-in-Chief, Prince of Huayuan.
Compiled by his Dharma-heir junior disciple, Shanguo, while residing at Mount Daoyi. Volume One.
On the day the Master opened the hall, he held up the incense and said:
"This one portion of incense is offered with devotion to pray for the Emperor’s sacred life to be infinite.

This one portion of incense is offered to serve the Prefect, the Academician, the various Surveillance Commissioners, and all the officials of the entire prefecture, that they may long remain in their positions of honor. This one portion of incense is the name of which neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs know."
"Human and celestial beings gaze upon him together. With a hand of faith, he brings forth exactly what is there—half a catty or eight taels.

Now, before this assembly of humans and devas, he shall no longer conceal or cover it. For the sake of Chan Master Yan, the tenth-generation descendant of Mount Wuzu in Qizhou, he burns this incense within the furnace to repay the milk of the Dharma.
Thereupon, he takes his seat. Master Daolin Yuanwu strikes the gavel and says: "The Dharma..."
He invited the assembly of dragon-elephants and said, "You should contemplate the primary truth (*paramārtha*). The Master asked, "If it is the primary truth, how then should one contemplate it?
After a long silence, he said, "In the kingdom of Magadha, this decree has already been issued; let us not obscure the ancestral style, but rather provide mutual verification."
If this is not yet so, and you have doubts, please ask. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the single melody of Yunmen;
what is the single melody of Baoci? The Master said, "Today is the first day of the third month. The monk said, "Do you permit me, your disciple, to join in the harmony?
The Master said, "How will you harmonize it? The monk clapped his hands. The Master said, "That is merely a guess; it has nothing to do with it. The monk... [remained silent].
The monk said, "When there is spirit, one adds to that spirit; where there is no elegance, one is elegant nonetheless. The Master said, "You are a guest under the gate of Beichan.
The monk said, "Within the domain of a patch-robed monk, there is the tongs and hammer for breaking through empty space, and the spirit that scatters white clouds.
Why is it that today you have no path for turning back? The Master said, "That is not within your realm."
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand whose realm this is. The Master said, "In the ordinary lowering of the hand, the ancient wind sweeps clear across the earth.
The monk said, "Were it not for posing this question, how could one discern the pivot of the Dharma King? The Master said, "I do not yet dare grant you permission."
The Master then said: "The Ultimate Way is profound and subtle; the path of names and words is cut off. The true source is serene and still;

both things and self are thus. Therefore it is said: before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from his mother’s womb, his work of saving beings was already complete.
Brightly manifest, the Great Matter was perfected; in silent stillness, he pervaded and penetrated the Dharma-realm. When he reached the interior of the Lumbinī Garden, he took seven steps around..."

Having already traversed the realms of transcendence and subtlety, how could one bear to look around? Yet, those of the Śrāvaka vehicle are rarely encountered, and those of like nature are difficult to harmonize.

Thus, I have yielded to human sentiments and observed the capacities of beings to benefit them. The Three Vehicles and Five Teachings have been disseminated throughout the world; as faculties and dispositions differ, there are variations in their ascent and descent.
Although it is a single voice that is proclaimed, sentient beings each attain understanding according to their own kind. [The six classes of ordinary beings and the four...]
Birth is manifested through this. The ultimate meaning transcends words and surpasses all conceptual proliferation.
Thus, from the beginning at the Deer Park to the end at the Bāhudā River—within these two intervals—he never spoke a single word. O practitioners of Chan:
if the texts and meanings in the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury are so brilliantly clear, why does he say he never spoke a single word? Is there anyone who...
There is no place to entrust it; here one perceives its seamless fusion. Penetrating beyond past and present, neither saint nor ordinary being need wait.
Amidst the three assemblies of the Dragon Flower, you stand upon the ground to instruct the sovereign; transcending the *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*, you proceed directly toward Bodhi.

Take this as a verification in the present moment, where illumination and function manifest simultaneously. Should your mind’s eye remain dim and obscured, you cannot avoid having to add further annotations. You must—
"Do you understand? In that year there was no preaching; it was where I heard it directly. A pure breeze pervades the nine realms" (the words of thanks are not recorded).
When the Master accepted an invitation at Chongning Temple, he held up a notice before the Dharma seat and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Fortunately, there is not a single thing."
The firm earth gives rise to waves; having reached such a state, it is difficult to avoid. I dare ask you all:
"The great earth does not admit even a needle—where did this come from? Do you understand? "The green mountains cannot hide it; the bright moon, however, admits it.
After handing [the robe] to the *vina* (karmadāna) to read, he then held up the robe and said: "On Mount Kukkuṭapāda, it was transmitted only to Kāśyapa."
On the dais at Huangmei, it was entrusted solely to Old Lu. Now that the time has arrived, it has fallen into the hands of this mountain monk.
Does the assembly know? Amidst the gathered necklaces, auspicious vapors soar; within the shadows of the flowered canopies, the fragrant spring is seized. Thereupon, he donned his robe.
Pointing to the seat, he said: "This is the throne of the Lamp King; vast and lofty through kalpas.
If you insist on ascending high, you are utterly failing to observe the proper season. Even so, there is another matter you have not yet seen: the white lotus blooms toward the mid-heavens."

He adjusted his robes, took his seat, and said: "Now that I have ascended this precious throne, a pure breeze rises from all four directions. The vital ford is firmly secured; both ordinary and sagely beings alike vanish.
I shall open a single thread of the Way to reveal my distinct style and regulations. Let any Zen person with eyes examine it as they please. A monk asked:
"I do not ask about turning iron into gold; how is it to transform the ordinary into the holy?
The Master said, "The staff has eyes as bright as the sun; to recognize true gold, look within the fire. The monk said, "For several days, auspicious birds have clamored by the courtyard;
indeed, the Prefect’s summons was most earnest. The Master said, "What a fine master you are, yet you have turned back within the flow of words. The monk said, [silently].
The ripening of the fruit of Bodhi is naturally distinct; the blooming of the utpala flower is a spring apart. The Master said: "A single word can wound a person;
it stirs the belly like a thousand blades. The Master then said: "It is easy to emerge from within the gate; it is difficult to exit from within the body.
At the place where ease and difficulty do not reach, let everyone join me in looking. He then raised his whisk and asked: "Do you see it? If you say you see it..."

What is meant by "seeing"? If you see, you remain an ordinary person, wandering aimlessly just like everyone else. If you say you do not see, how can you not see? Where are the eyes of a high-minded traveler?
How can one clearly distinguish between seeing and not seeing? Only when you have reached thorough penetration here [can you know].
The pivot of the Tathāgatas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs has, throughout their lives, been like ice melting and a gate dismantled.
If this is not yet so, I shall take the unperforated flute of Shaolin and blow for you the "Little Yangchun. [Having descended from the seat, the words of thanks are not recorded.]

That night, during the informal sermon (*xiaochan*), [the Master said]: "When the total function is not employed, only those on the same path will know it. When illumination and function proceed together, who can fully comprehend it?
Therefore, Master Bajiao addressed the assembly, saying: 'If you have a staff, I shall give you a staff.'"
"You have no staff; I shall take away your staff. The Master said, "Bajiao’s model is rarely met with by those who understand it, past or present.
Later, Chan Master Juehai commented: "If you have a staff, I take away your staff;
if you have no staff, I give you a staff. Chan Master Juehai was truly one of great measure.
As soon as you are appointed to office, you measure your feet to buy boots; yet, if you wish to see the plantain tree, it seems you will not yet be able to.
If you were Xinfobao Ci, it would not be so: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; a gentleman loves wealth, but takes it by the right means.
If you have no staff, I take away your staff. When the kindness is deep, one becomes speechless in one's heart.
This is self-evident. Suddenly, a man comes forward and asks: "Apart from these two paths, what is the staff of Baozi?

After a long silence, he says: "Now it stands planted atop Mount Sumeru; even those with six arms and three heads are not permitted to look. Having stood for a long time, I bid you all adieu. Be well.

I bid farewell to Elder Xuan as he departs to reside at Ciyun Monastery. The secret intent of Vulture Peak and the profound essence of Shaoshi—these five leaves and one flower have been distributed throughout the dust-motes of all lands.

Those who realize this intent move with ease through the myriad functions of existence, unfolding and rolling up [the teachings] without obstruction. Those who lose its true direction may discuss the truth, yet remain like a phantom image; their understanding becomes biased and stunted.
Have you not seen how even the "Holy Arrow" from within the city found it necessary to traverse the rugged terrain of Mount Gu? The State...
The Master held the numinous talisman behind his elbow; even Danyuan remained in doubt as to whether to stay or go. "Great assembly, what would you do at such a moment if you were Xingbao Ci?
Although it was as impenetrable as water-tight sealing, one cannot help but swing one's arms while walking.
He then raised his whisk and said: "Do you see? I present this whisk made of tortoise hair as a gift, to point the way for the traveler."
Head. On that day, he ascended the hall: "This ancient temple of Baoci is the site of former sages. Its gate rests against the Xiang River; surely there are many fishermen here.
Moreover, with the wind calm and the waves still, it is precisely the right time to cast the line. Is there anyone? A monk stepped forward and said, "Not running downhill! [The Master] said, "Quick!"
"It is indeed difficult to encounter," the Master said. "As expected. A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest?
The Master said, "This year’s poverty is like last year’s poverty. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "The army follows the seal; the general pursues the tally.
The monk asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "Casting off precious and noble robes, one puts on tattered and soiled garments."
The monk asked, "What is the master among masters? The Master said, "Lying across the body to face the universe—who is the one who emerges?
The monk said, "I have received the teacher’s instruction regarding the four guests and hosts; as for the profound mystery beyond, what is it like?

The Master said, "One battle, two battles, and the clear wind arises, blowing away thousands of fragments of white clouds. The monk said, "The peak where the bowl was cast is magnificent... [The text ends here.]

"High for ten thousand ages, it is passed down through the generations. The Master said: "If you do not see what has been gathered before and after, how can you diligently entrust it for later generations to behold?
The Master then said: "If one were to fully uphold the Patriarchal Command, the entire great earth would become desolate.

If one were to merely level the high by following the low, it would serve only as a wall and moat for my own house. Therefore it is said: 'The path that points upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages. If you intend to..."
In the midst of this deliberation, they alternate as host and guest. When he acts as the host, he seizes the vital ford so that both sages and ordinary people are lost;

the celestial demons’ hearts shatter as he strides alone across the earth. When he acts as the guest, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, trees, and forests—the myriad phenomena in their full array—all manifest his wondrous essence.
Although it is thus, how can one express the single phrase that does not fall into the categories of host and guest?
He gave rise to the Way. After a long silence, he said: "A single mass of white clouds stretches across the universe; throughout the heavens, there is nowhere it does not cast its shade.

(The words of thanks are not recorded. That night, during the informal discourse (*xiao-can*), he said: "To meet the challenge with one's full capacity is rarely encountered in all antiquity. To 'crack' and 'peck' simultaneously is not yet being a master hand."
Only when one does not reveal their sharp edge can they truly be called a man of stature; it is not enough to merely boast of one's own strategies if one is not the true master of the house.
Have you not seen how Zhaozhou, upon meeting an old woman on the road, asked, "Where are you going? and the woman replied, "I am going to steal Zhaozhou’s bamboo shoots"?
Zhaozhou said, "What is it like when you suddenly encounter Zhaozhou? The old woman then gave him a slap. Zhaozhou stopped and withdrew. Later, Xuedou commented, "A fine slap!
But even if he were given two more slaps, there would still be no place for examination. The Master said, "All you Zen practitioners, tell me: where does the error lie?
Baoci will now try to deliberate with you all on this. One person is accustomed to walking along the narrow mountain paths."
Having experienced the frontier courts to the full, not a single blade was drawn; the seas were calm and the rivers clear. One person acted as the vanguard, while none followed from the rear.
"To covet another’s cup of wine, one loses the fish in the entire boat. Tell me, where did Baoci’s act of benefiting others fall? Do you understand?
The sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice; the medicine emerges from the golden jar to save the sick.
The next day, Administrative Head Xie ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all dust motes.
Holding up his sitting cloth, he said, "This is the dust; which one is the firm and dense body? The Master said, "Put it down.
The monk said, "This is still where the student has doubts. The Master said, "What are your doubts? The monk said, "Just now..."
The questioner asked about the bottom [of the matter]. The Master said, "He is not fit to be used as fodder. The Master then continued, "Just now, this monk asked:
'The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all dust. I, the mountain monk, answered him thus. Now tell me: did this monk know it, or did he not?
If you say he knew it, why would he have dared to ask such a question? If you say he did not know it, how could he have understood enough to ask in such a way?"
"O virtuous practitioners of dhyāna! When you arrive here, how do you distinguish and clarify it? Whether you know or do not know, you possess no skill at all.
I shall clearly proclaim the intent of the teaching; I shall gently strike and sing for you. Thereupon, he raised his whisk and said:
"O assembly! This is the firm and dense body. From where could all these dust motes have come? If you gain a sudden flash of insight here, not only..."
Walking alone through the misty clouds, he likewise provides external protection for the monastic groves. Should this not yet be clear, I cannot help but provide further annotation.
Do you wish to understand? The wind stirs the vast sky, and spring clouds rise from all sides. Those with six arms and three heads may boast of their clever tongues in vain;
throughout the earth and under heaven, there is no one who can truly be a peer. I casually bring this forth for you to behold—recognize it clearly and directly right now!
He took it and, tossing down his whisk, returned to the Abbot’s quarters for a small session (xiaocan).
He said: "The secret key of all Buddhas and the original source of all living beings—how could they ever be fully proclaimed even from the dragon palaces within the ocean-treasury? Why is this so?"
True permanence is signless, yet wondrous existence is all-encompassing. In every land and every atom, it pervades the entire Dharma-realm.
Why labor over cultivation when essence and function are so clearly manifest? Returning directly to this very moment, what further matter remains?

Have you not seen how a monk asked Muzhou Shanzhao, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Muzhou remained silent. The monk shook his sleeves and departed, arriving at Xuefeng. Xuefeng—
He then asked, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Gui. Feng asked, "What words did Mount Gui have to show his disciples?
The monk said, "I once asked him, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? and Mount Gui remained silent. Feng said, "Do you approve of him?
The monk said, "I do not approve of him. Feng said, "Mount Gui is an ancient Buddha; go quickly and pay him homage."
He performed prostrations and repented. Later, Xuansha heard of this and said, "That old fellow on the mountain head has botched the public case of Master Muzhou.
The monk then asked, "What was your honorable intention, Master? Xuansha said, "Great Muzhou was reduced to a hundred fragments by this monk’s single question.
The Master said, "All you Zen practitioners, let us set aside for a moment the fact that this monk ran south and fled north; what about Xuansha acting in such a manner?"
"What do you say? Is this a word of praise, or is it a word of refusal? You practitioners from the Five Lakes and the eminent masters of the four seas—try to discern and clarify this for me!
To see the Truth here is not only to have the Eye of the School clearly open, but it is also to sit upon the tongues of all the old monks of the world.
Nevertheless, if one does not enter the great waves, how can one see the one who plays with the tide?"
Ascending the hall to address the assembly: The melody of the stringless lute rarely meets with a connoisseur; within the forest of no-shadows, it is difficult to find footprints.
Only those of like voice and breath can discern the initial signs; otherwise, one who is not of the house will labor in vain by prying their ears.
Have you not seen how Nanquan asked Huangbo, "The equal study of concentration and wisdom leads to the clear realization of Buddha-nature—what is the principle behind this? Huangbo replied, "Ten..."
"During these two times [of eating], one does not rely upon a single thing. Baizhang said, "Is this perhaps the Elder’s own view? Huangbo said, "I dare not say so.
Huangbo continued, "Let us set aside the cost of the gruel and rice for now; who will repay the cost of the straw sandals? Huangbo then desisted.

The Master said: "All you practitioners of Chan: Nanquan and Huangbo were much like two armies burying their weapons and engaging in combat. When the two forces clash, is there a distinction of superior or inferior?
If you say there is, this person has not yet attained the eye of a traveling monk. If you say there is not, this person has not yet attained the eye of a traveling monk.
If it is neither of these, then how is it? Do you wish to understand? It is like a jade seal that does not..."
Once it leaves the hands of a celestial king, how could an ordinary person ever know the contents of this golden casket?

When the patron invites you to ascend the hall, the disciples under Kāśyapa merely boast of the "smile" kōan; those before the cliff of Shaoshi Rock vainly discourse on the method of "settling the mind.
How can these compare to the oars and paddles displayed upon a light, painted boat—where ten thousand *li* are clear of clouds and the sky is forever vast?
Heaven and earth are of one color. In reed-banked coves and moonlit islets, fishermen cast their lines; amidst misty islands and the heart of the waves, shorebirds play in the sunlight.
Leisurely brewing green tea, they pour themselves full cups of flowing rosy clouds. Vast is the imperial wind; level is the sovereign way. A few notes from a returning flute leave the spring harbor;
a single solitary sail passes through the cavernous ferry. To leave the boat upon reaching the shore is but a constant practice—what need is there to ask further?
"O people at the ferryhead! All you virtuous Chan practitioners, when Baozi spoke and sang thus, was there still a place where he acted for the sake of others?
If you say there was, where exactly was that place? If you say there was not, then by beating the drum and ascending the hall, he would have failed his host.
At this point, how can one reveal it? Do you understand? (Pauses) After a long silence, he says: 'A person returns to the great kingdom only then to become a vessel; when the water reaches..."
The vast ocean begins with waves.
Entering the hall: When a chess player meets a worthy opponent, even the most secret moves cannot be hidden; when a lute meets a connoisseur, its subtle resonance is revealed.
The true command of Makara is known only by those on the same path. To grasp and release, to awaken the deluded with a single decision—have you not seen what Qianfeng showed?
The assembly said, "If you raise one, you cannot; if you raise two, you let it pass. One point falls into the second.
Yunmen stepped forward and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went back to Jingshan. Feng then said, "The head cook, do not call for a communal work assignment tomorrow.
He then descended from his seat. The Master said, "One person exerts their utmost effort for the sake of the multitude, yet the disaster emerges from the private door. One person...
The eyes emit flashes of lightning that pierce through the four continents. Now tell me: which phrase is the guest? Which phrase is the host?
If one can discern this, the heels of their straw sandals will snap off and they will pass through the patriarch’s barrier.
If you have not yet reached this point, it is easier to turn iron into gold than it is to exhort others to abandon their attachments to right and wrong.
On account of a certain matter, he ascended the hall and said: "The mouth born of one's parents—how could it hinder one from speaking for one’s child?
Do not hang trivial matters upon your mind; this is precisely the auspicious season of the human world.

Suddenly, there was a man who, hearing Kaifu speak thus, came forth from the assembly, pointed his finger at him, and said, "Old and decrepit as you are, you have not rid yourself of vulgarity. The Master laughed heartily and said, "You merely..."
When one beholds the clear wind and white moon, how could one fail to know the fragrance of flowers within the cave? Why is this so?
Having once watched those who play in the tide upon the river, one has never heard them love the water and loathe the waves.

One day, the Master ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "That which not a thousand sages have transmitted, the secret words of all the patriarchs—I shall now reveal for you, sparing not even my eyebrows.
When the patch-robed monks lift their eyes, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The one essential point of Baozi is wondrous for both ordinary and holy beings alike. The barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys; the dragon’s roar and the tiger’s cry;
the Daoist priest delighting in the spirits and the shaman sacrificing at the temple. When the rain has passed, the mountains are green;

when the clouds have withdrawn, the sun shines. Shide and Hanshan cannot help but laugh 'he-he. Zen masters, tell me, what are they laughing at? Enough, enough! In years to come, you will know for yourselves."
Sound! How could it wait for this morning to be explained?

On the Winter Solstice, ascending the hall: As the movements of the celestial sphere shift and the sun reaches its longest path southward, there is clearly a single ray of grace that shines through the ten directions and the three periods of time, fully revealing the profound pivot of the patriarchs and leaking forth the very core of the monks’ realization. Lingyun bluntly said:
There is no doubt. Maitreya’s boasting of his prediction of enlightenment—how can it compare to Li Si and Zhang San congratulating one another from street to alley?
This is neither the radiance of the Sea-Seal Samādhi nor the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. You lofty men of the forest, do not indulge in such drowsiness!
Causing others to smile with uplifted brows in the midst of darkness; truly, this pure wind moves heaven and earth. *Small Session* (Xiao-can):
The profound essence of the School Gate is rarely mastered by those who enter it. When essence and function are impartial, one attains the wondrous as they flow along with the current.

At times, they act as both host and guest, striking and singing the mysterious wind; at other times, they hide their bodies face-to-face, making their traces difficult to discern. This is the critical ford.
He cuts off the source of delusion for both ordinary beings and sages; bestowing compassion to benefit all, he enters the weeds with ease.
Have you not seen the old woman on the road to Mount Tai? Whenever a monk asked her, "Where does the road to Mount Tai go? the woman would say, "Go straight ahead.
As soon as the monk departed, she would say, "What a fine master, yet he goes away like that. When Zhaozhou heard of this, he went there.
A monk asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai lead? The old woman said, "Go straight ahead. As soon as the monk departed, the old woman said, "What a fine master you are, yet you go off like that!
Upon returning to the monastery, the monk informed the assembly, saying, "I have thoroughly exposed this old woman for you all.
The Master said, "Vast and open, without deviation; clear and bright, penetrating past and present. When asked, he had no other words; his answer was simply this.
Is this not a different sound? Where is the point of realization? Do you understand thoroughly? One person hoists the sail; another grips the rudder.
The iron flute is blown crosswise; the fisherman’s song is sung in harmony. In the simultaneous act of pecking and piercing, how many are true connoisseurs?
Returning against the current or with the flow, it is only upon reaching the shore that one truly knows it is not so. It is not so—I proclaim it for you: sweet as sand.

The Master said, “You head toward Xiangxiang, while I go to Qin. The Master then said, “The true decree of Mahākāśyapa could not avoid its rugged path;
the compassion bestowed at Shaoshi Mountain already wounded the very bones and marrow. Carrying the satchel and grasping the staff, one fails the peace of mind.”
Birth! Refining practice and extinguishing the mind lead one another toward dullness. How can this compare to a spring rain clearing away, leaving the spring mountains green?
Three clouds, five clouds; a warbler’s call, two calls. The Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot gaze enough; though Wang Wei was skilled, he could not have captured it in a painting.
Even if you were to act just so, you would still be traversing a path. O Zen practitioners, do not traverse a path.
"How do you express it in a single phrase? After a long silence, he said: "A person comes from Bianzhou, yet receives no news from Dongjing.

The patron has requested that I ascend the seat to recite the *Tripitaka* for repentance. Before this Elder has even left the abbot's quarters, the sound of the drum has already proclaimed the perfect resonance.
To hear with the eyes and see with the ears is not a matter of something external; why then must one laboriously seek elsewhere? O Zen practitioners, this is so.
"How do you understand hearing with the eyes? How do you understand seeing with the ears?

If you can realize this here and now, within the realm of Vairocana the ancient Buddhas radiate light, and amidst the thicket of thorns the Prajñā is proclaimed. Without shifting a single step, one sits in the Great Dharma Assembly.
If, however, you are like one grasping at the moon in the waves or seeking fish by climbing a tree—your wild mind not yet stilled—I pray you will submit your questions. The monk [asked].
The monk asked, "What is the full functioning of Linji? The Master said, "Where have you come from?

Sitting in meditation amidst the crags while the Lord of Heaven scatters flowers; where there is neither speech nor hearing, one hides the head and reveals the shadow. At Shaolin, facing the wall, he merely engaged in calculation."
It was not yet accomplished. Standing in the snow to sever his own arm, he brought shame upon other monastics; at Huangmei, presenting a verse, his victory and defeat were lopsided.

Though such are the transgressions that fill the heavens, were it not for the patrons who provide the call and response, how could one see those present at the Dragon Flower Assembly?
I have stood for a long time before you, O compassionate ones; I pray you all take care of yourselves.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Traveling monks who brush aside the weeds and observe the wind have not yet passed through the barrier before their eyes; it is difficult for them to clarify the seal of the mind-ground.
Have you not seen what the former sages said? 'If you wish to recognize the mind of all Buddhas, simply seek it within the mental activities of sentient beings.'"
One must recognize the nature that is eternally abiding and never decaying; seek it only within the place where the myriad phenomena undergo transformation.

All you practitioners of Chan: once a word has been uttered, even four horses cannot overtake it. Shift the pivot of the profound mystery and penetrate the ultimate reality. If you can gain conviction here—
Within the realm of worldly toil, the profound mystery of the thousand sages is suddenly unveiled; amidst the cycle of prosperity and decline, one directly realizes the true face of many lifetimes.

Transcending the shore of awakening without relying on gradual cultivation—yet, should one’s doubts remain unresolved or one’s views be biased and stunted, do not mistake a three-year-old bamboo for a ten-thousand-year-old pine. (Striking the meditation seat, he rolls up the scroll.)
The Recorded Sayings of the Nineteenth Abbot, Master Ning, of Kaifu Chan Monastery in Tanzhou, Volume II.
Compiled by his Dharma-heir junior disciple, Shanguo, while residing at Mount Daomei.
Ascending the Hall: The spring breeze blows gently; the spring days are bright and pleasant. A bird sings atop the eastern ridge; flowers bloom upon the southern branches of the trees.
In the gardens and along the purple thoroughfares, the enjoyment of these sights is most fitting. The passersby are half-drunk and half-awake; the travelers appear dazed and delirious.
Whether singing or dancing, laughing or weeping—every single instance is the business of our house; everywhere, the wondrous *dhāraṇī* is fully revealed.
Why, then, do you seize upon this and give rise to doubt? You thus fail the ancient masters who exerted themselves to lay it bare.
If you do not comprehend this meaning, your practice will be nothing but bitter toil. I shall now take my leave; may the assembly remain in good health.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "Yongjia said: 'People do not recognize the mani jewel; it is personally held within the Tathāgatagarbha.'"
[The monk] did not ask about the *tathāgatagarbha*. [The monk asked: "Which one is the pearl? The Master said: "Sometimes I idly carry it on the tip of my staff;
the Thousand-Eyed Great Compassionate One cannot see it. The monk said: "I thought the news of Shaolin had been cut off, but now its traces remain perfectly intact.
The Master said: "Why do you not ask about the *tathāgatagarbha*? The monk said: "Having grasped the horn of the black dragon, I have snatched it away."
The monk returned with a bright pearl. The Master asked, "Where is the pearl? The monk lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). The Master said, "Not yet a skilled hand. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "To change according to the occasion. A monk asked, "As the light of time slips away and the years grow cold, the Chan school has won the opportunity to engage in discourse together.
No one understands the message within this; I wish to hear you proclaim the ancestral patriarch’s barrier."
The Master said, "An iron ox blocks the ancient road. The monk asked, "Is this not where you, Master, guide people?
The Master said, "The Great Way before one's eyes has no detours; why do you wander aimlessly seeking it elsewhere?
The monk said, "Today I have received a true message: white snow and plum blossoms fill the cave. The Master said, "Do not savor idle phrases."
"Ancestor’s Mind. The Master then said: "The quiescent nature of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words.

What was the purpose of all those questions and answers just now? Do you understand thoroughly? For one who has attained penetration, verbal expression and silent silence both return to the field of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
For beginners and even those of high standing, they instead become methods of acceptance and rejection. Gardens, groves, ponds, and marshes all expound [the Dharma]."
“Wondrous Sound! All phenomena that arise are manifested solely by the mind. Furthermore, it is neither the wind moving nor the banner moving;
it is you, O virtuous one, whose mind moves. All you venerable practitioners of Zen: the Great and Little Old Lūs deserve thirty blows each. Why?

Because they know only how to put on their boots, yet fail to notice their trousers have torn. Nevertheless, though it is so, the singing of birds is much the same everywhere, and the falling of flowers is no different.”

Hearing the sound of flowing water, he ascended the hall to instruct the assembly: "If you have not yet passed through the Patriarch’s barrier, time flies as swiftly as an arrow. White hair grows in its full brilliance;
it is already the fifth day of the New Year. I recall Yunmen saying, 'On level ground there are countless dead people,' yet one must still pass through the thorny brambles."
Linji was a master of his craft. At that time, a monk asked him, "In that case, the first seat in the hall must have great merit.
Yunmen said, "Suru suru. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "He casually extends his hand, and a pure breeze arises from all eight directions.
Nevertheless, even so, when scrutinized closely, great Yunmen was squeezed by this monk."
He has truly reached a state where there is no way to hide his body. Do you all see it?

If you can perceive this clearly here, you will see that there are countless living beings upon the level ground, turning the Great Dharma Wheel even amidst the thorny thickets. Why is this? Because the Great Compassionate One does not extend his hand.
The whole body is eyes. (He strikes the meditation seat.

He thanks the guest prefect and ascends the hall. Opening the door, he awaits the man of knowledge; yet the man of knowledge does not come to pass by. Since the man of knowledge has already passed by, upon what basis can one provide an arrangement?
Early in the morning the golden fruit is plucked by the monkey; late in the evening the jade flower is carried away by the phoenix. And so it is.
Transcending the subtle and the minute, he did not employ martial arts; yet it is rare to encounter one who truly understands him.
Have you not seen how Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you been here before? The monk replied, "I have. Zhaozhou said, "Go drink tea. Zhaozhou then asked another monk, "Have you been here before?
The monk replied, "I have not. Zhaozhou said, "Go drink tea. When the monastery attendant asked Zhaozhou about this, Zhaozhou replied, "He has been here before."
"Teach him to go drink tea"—let that be for now. But why, when he had never been to this place before, did he tell him to go drink tea?
The Governor called for the head monk; the monk responded. The Governor said, "Go drink tea. The Master said: "Under Zhaozhou’s gate, there is no discrimination between high and low;
a single bowl of coarse tea is offered universally. Only those who attain its flavor will know the nine-fold transformation within cold ashes."

Incense from the bottle has permeated. If you have yet to discern the beginning and end of this matter, I cannot help but provide another annotation: "North, south, east, and west—ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand.
Zhaozhou’s reception of guests was by no means in vain. Do not disdain its lack of flavor or its coldness; he is accustomed to frying sesame seeds all at once.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Only the adamantine eye remains, which Zen practitioners from the four seas chew upon. If they can chew it through, the ignorance of kalpas will be instantly incinerated, and they will enjoy sovereign bliss in heaven and among men.
If they cannot chew it through, they form knots and fetters; at the gates of the six sense-faculties, the conditions of dust and circumstance compete to arise."
Chan virtue! You chew on it; set it aside in a quiet place. Radiant and flawless, its brilliance flashes forth.
How many times has it been presented face-to-face? It is simply that people themselves avoid it.

Ascending the hall to address the assembly: Truth does not conceal falsehood; the crooked does not hide the straight. Within every phrase, the person is revealed; amidst every word, the essential point is discerned.
In every place, total mastery is maintained; at every turn, it is Maitreya. To deliberate or reflect is to encounter thorns at one’s own gate.

Have you not seen how the Ancient Virtuous One asked a monk, "What sound is that in the grove? The monk replied, "The sound of a magpie. The Ancient Virtuous One said, "If you wish not to incur [retribution]..."

Regarding the karma of immediate retribution: do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. All you virtuous ones in meditation, even if your entire bodies were mouths, how would you deliberate upon this?
Do you wish to understand? A path leads secretly through the mountains; flowers flow forth from within the cavern.
Master Xie Huanzhu returned to the monastery and ascended the hall. The Master said, "Zen practitioners, do not be reckless. It is the fifth day of the second month.
Having thoroughly penetrated the barrier of the Patriarchs, a single phrase encompasses both the present and antiquity.
Even so, how would you deliberate upon that matter which does not involve the present or antiquity? Is there anyone who knows it? Come forward and reveal it. A monk asked, "What about [this]?"
"This is the guest among guests. The Master said, "The traveler on the road asks for the ford again.
The monk asked, "What is the host among guests? The Master said, "You, Reverend, should tell it yourself. The monk asked, "What is the guest among hosts?
The Master said, "The question is clear; the answer is most intimate. The monk asked, "What is the host among hosts? The Master said, "The radiance of the seven stars shines forth."
The six states ceased their smoke and dust. A monk asked, "Beyond the four types of guest and host, is there anything further? The Master said, "Even looking inward, there is nothing.
The monk said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "This is not within your realm. The Master then said: "The spring colors have no high or low;
The garden trees and flowers are red. The Gate of Total Retention stands wide open; Where can one seek Perfect Penetration? Do not ask about delusion."
Upon meeting Bodhidharma, you must know that he extended his hand into the midst of the dust, trampled the thick earth, and pierced through empty space.

He was one who dares to compete in wealth with the Dragon King, hanging out a notice for devas and humans, and manifesting the ancestral style of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Saving both self and others, his merit is inexhaustible;
turning his body about, he leaves no trace, ascending directly to the wondrous high peak. O practitioners of Zen, tell me: whose realm is this? Do you understand?
Simma! He has no face; he takes the three realms as his home. Able to wield the staff over his head, he encounters spring and dots the extraordinary flowers.
On this year-end small *paramārtha* (small *śamaya*), time passes swiftly, making no appointment with man; in an instant one world changes, and already the year’s end is seen.
As long as the ground of the mind is not clearly realized, doubt is unavoidable.
Even if one’s questions were like a hundred rivers rushing together and one’s answers like the great ocean swallowing all streams, they would be of no use within the hall of the ancient Buddhas.

It is like a fragment of cloud appearing in the vast clarity of the sky. A monk asked, "In that case, does the vast clarity itself receive this mark?
Lingyun did not answer. The monk said, "If so, then do sentient beings not come forth? Lingyun did not answer.
The monk asked, "When one has attained such pure clarity where all marks are extinguished, what then? Lingyun said, "This is still the flow of the eternal and constant. The monk asked, "What is it?"
The true and eternal flow continues. Lingyun said, "It is like a mirror that is constantly bright. A monk asked, "Is there still something above this?
Lingyun said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is this thing above? Lingyun said, "Break the mirror and then I will see you.
The Master then said, "Excellent, all you virtuous Chan practitioners! The entire world of the ten directions is a single mirror. Make—"

How can one explain the principle of "breaking through"? Reaching this point, even if you have eyes that see clearly and hands that discern with precision, such that light and shadow both vanish—like a hen brooding her eggs, where the pecking and the breaking are simultaneous—you are precisely fit to receive the staff of Baoci. Why?
Because Zen practitioners who dally with shadows are as numerous as hemp and millet; though they gain no real power, they are still better than those who labor their minds elsewhere.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests in thousands, tens of billions of bodies, constantly showing himself to the people of the world, yet the people do not recognize him.
I wonder, does the Master recognize him? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, do not recognize him.
The monk said, "How is it that the great Baoci does not recognize him? The Master said, "The old monk does not conceal this matter. The monk said, "He has been seen through."
"It is understood. The Master said, "Thirty years hence, you will suddenly break into a sweat; it is not yet certain. The Master then said:

"To engage in sharp and novel questions and answers, displaying lofty faculties, is like using painted cakes to satisfy hunger. Even if one passes through kalpas as numerous as dust motes, such toil is in vain.

How can this compare to forgetting words and merging with the Great Void? Why is this so? The wondrous purport of the Patriarchs is remote and beyond verbal expression; it is a secret resonance with the Mystical Source."
To achieve much too early leads to many complications; how much more so when one recklessly presents one's own views, making it impossible to distinguish between the ordained and the laity?
Brandishing the sharp blades of rhetoric, they compete over right and wrong, and those who wish to investigate this school are driven ever further away. Nevertheless, though it be thus:
"The moon in the empty realm of the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after repeatedly stirring and searching will one finally know it."
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: The radiant scenery leaves no room for neglect; one need not see Danxia burn the Buddha.
Do not say that opening the furnace has nothing to do; Fenyang waves his fan in his hand. O Zen adepts, the secret intent of the Patriarchs is remote and free from even a speck of dust;
its application is impartial and does not fail the seasons. When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot. The wooden Buddha emits...
Radiant light! The master of the monastery felt great joy; a silk fan provided sufficient cool breeze, yet the patch-robed monk could not shake it.
This is clearly a matter of leaking out the celestial mechanism—why do you fail to perceive it? If the profound pivot is turned, the eye-mind will naturally open wide;
only then will you believe that the events of the distant *Putong* era did not come from being carried over the Xiangling Pass.
Master Xie, the Librarian, ascends the hall: "The soldiers follow the seal’s turn; the generals pursue the talisman’s path. When the vital pass is firmly blocked, no news may pass through.
Yet, affairs are never one-sided and principles emerge from many gates. Borrowing this path to pass by, I shall briefly meet with you all.
I recall that in the past, Yantou, Xuefeng, and Qinshan—these three—were traveling together when they reached a mountain temple and encountered rain."
Every day, Qingshan and Xuefeng were looking through the Tripitaka, while Yantou sat silently and upright.
The Librarian asked Yantou, "In this place, we receive guests and encourage them to look at the scriptures to form karmic connections.
Yet you, Venerable Sir, sit upright and meditate after eating your meal; what benefit or salvation do you provide? Yantou replied, "I am illiterate. The Librarian said, "Why then..."
He questioned a person. Yan then took up a scroll of scripture and pointed to two strokes (丿) at the title, asking the Librarian, "What character is this?
The Librarian replied, "I do not know this character. Yan said, "If you do not even know this character, what is the point of reading the sutra?
He then brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master then said, "All you Zen practitioners: Yan-tou’s display of brilliance for a time was much like greedily watching a white..."
The waves have caused the loss of the oar; the Abbot has won a stroke in the dark. Few people, ancient or modern, know this.
As for the saying, "It is not formed by the character 'yi' (以), nor is it the character 'ba' (八)," what character is it ultimately called?
If you can see into this here, not only will you pierce through the nostrils of Yantou, but the entire Great Canon (*Tripitaka*) will be revealed from within. If this is not yet so, [you are lost].
I shall spare you the trouble of adding further annotations. The character "yi" (以) is not the "ba" (八) that fails to form [the word].
The Silent Child laughs with joy; the *udumbara* flower appears as an auspicious omen in the human world. His nostrils pierce through to the heavens, yet he does not smell. O practitioners of Zen:
since his nostrils pierce through to the heavens, why does he not smell? Do you wish to understand? Where the sun and moon do not reach, it is exceptionally fine and dry.

Kūn. The donor requests the Master to ascend the hall and address the assembly: "The Xiang Mountains are green; the Xiang River is azure. Above, below, and in the four quarters—east, west, south, and north—everywhere is Śākyamuni, every place is Maitreya.
When the hen pecks and the chick breaks open the shell simultaneously, there is no need for external seeking. See it here!"
It is attained. Without waiting for the kalpas of the *saṃgha* to be fulfilled or the merits of the six perfections to be perfected, how could one allow for deliberation at the site of the Way?
Yet, as doubts have not yet been shed and the power of faith remains incomplete, the clergy and laity present at the assembly request that you provide a clarifying discourse.

A monk asked: "The donor has respectfully extended three requests; with what Dharma will the Master benefit humans and devas? The Master said: "The pure wind rises from the four quarters, and the clouds—"

[The incense] wafts through the vast sky. The monk asked, "I do not know what kind of karmic reward the donor shall obtain. The Master said, "One merely attains karma in which the three spheres are pure;
its utility will be inexhaustible for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The Master then said, "Before the first signs of manifestation arise, the adornments are already fully complete."
As soon as heaven and earth were first divided, one had already entered upon a circuitous path. The profound barrier of Mahākāla was unfathomable to those of the age;
the edicts of Shaolin caused all things to fall like grass before the wind. To attempt to receive the transmission directly still results in a mere reflection;

how much more so to gather flowers into brocade, to turn jade and roll pearls, or to display a fountain of eloquence in an effort to exhaust the wondrous Way? This is very much like using a conch shell to scoop up the ocean or breaking off a blade of grass to measure the void.
To waste one's spirit and energy in this way is entirely without benefit. Why? If you seek understanding through words, you will be needlessly separated from the West.
(With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended.)
Giving thanks for the Dharma drum offered by a patron, he ascends the hall and says: "The true essence of the teaching in this land is pure within sound.
Those who wish to enter samādhi must truly realize it through hearing. O virtuous practitioners of Chan: as soon as the Dharma drum is struck, the humans and devas prick up their ears."
"Miraculous response without partiality—what is the essential purport here? If you can realize it at this very moment, the entire assembly at the Śūraṅgama Sūtra remains vividly present.
Do you all understand? The profound, perfect sound encompasses the Dharma-realm, directly awakening the deluded masses throughout ten thousand ages."

Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Torrential rain falls from the heavens; the temple bell rings out clearly and resonantly. In a realm where neither ear nor eye can reach, I feel a deep affinity for the old man who sat facing the wall.
Virtuous practitioners of Zen: This is the essential gateway of all Buddhas and the lineage of the Patriarchs. Yet the myriad beings within the Dharma-realm stubbornly refuse to acknowledge it.
Consequently, even the patch-robed monks of the Five Lakes and those of lofty character beyond the mundane world must carry their staffs and alms bowls to famous mountains and caves.

For some, it has been winter and summer, or spring and autumn; they merely know how to manipulate the source of their rhetoric and polish their lips and beaks, contending for supremacy and competing for sharpness as if it were their own family tradition.
Their ailment has reached the vital organs, and worldly physicians fold their hands in helplessness.

Fortunately, there is a wise person who appears in the world, bestowing compassion upon all beings. Before a peak ten thousand fathoms high, he casts his entire body down. Have you not seen the monk ask Xiyuan?
When Master Cong was about to ask, "What is it like when one does not ask?", Xiyuan struck him immediately.
As the monk hesitated, Xiyuan said, "If you understand this as being a blow from a staff, your eyebrows and whiskers will fall out. The monk had an awakening. O Zen adepts, do you know?

This monk actually possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger, yet Xiyuan unwittingly threw himself into its deep pit. If anyone can discern this, they will personally wear the *vimalakīrti* (the pure fame) upon their person.
Lu Yin plucked the tiger’s whiskers on the spot; yet, his understanding was not yet perfect. The staff has eyes as bright as the sun;
one must recognize true gold by looking at it in the fire.

Ascending the hall, he said: "In the dark, one draws out the transverse bone; in the light, one sits upon the tongue. Where neither partiality nor fullness reaches—ten thousand ages and a thousand autumns.

But tell me, what season is this? Can you discern it clearly? If you see it here, you need not wait for the three great kalpas to be fulfilled or the six perfections to be cultivated through熏修 (xūnxīu).
You will stand upon the spot and participate with the Buddhas of antiquity, suddenly realizing the true face of many lifetimes."
If your wisdom-eye has not yet become clear, you cannot avoid merely throwing sand and shaking dust.

Have you not seen how a monk asked Master Kaixian, "What is it like when the year is spent and the end of winter has come? Kaixian replied, "It is still as cold as in the early spring. O virtuous practitioners of Zen!
The models established by the former sages have been passed down through the human world. As days and years have deepened, Zen practitioners have neglected them.

Why is this? Their words are not mysterious or subtle; they simply penetrate the heavy barrier. When the painted vase is shattered, there is only clear water and green mountains. Do not be surprised that Baozi was so cold and aloof;
when one finds a place to linger, one should simply linger.
Ascending the hall: The majestic wind of the profound mystery, the samādhi of every dust mote—picking it up with the hand at random, there is never any obstruction.

No need for contrivance; from the start, there is neither aversion nor attachment. To pass through this barrier is to be carefree and sovereign. Yet to go about in such a manner already involves rugged difficulties.
To wait further for deliberation is to fail those former patriarchs. Nevertheless, within suchness, where is the capacity of those of inferior or middling faculties?
A rough sketch. This second thematic gate is briefly set forth for proclamation. I recall Furi asking Jia Shan: "The assembly gazes upward in expectation;
I beg the Master for a single word. Jia Shan said: "If you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket. Furi said: "Holding the Night-Bright Talisman in hand, how many know the dawn? Jia Shan said: "The assembly, return!"
"Coming and going—there is already someone who has realized it. The Master said: "A vast marsh hides a mountain; its principle can subdue even a leopard.
Although the needle and the mustard seed meet, tell me, where does it land? If you can see it here, the sun and moon are newly forged and heaven and earth are specially established.
If this is not yet so, the young maiden has already departed for the celestial heights, while the foolish lad still plays with the smoke from the brazier."

Winter Night Small Sermon: The ancient sages established their models with such exquisite skill that they could, as the occasion required, prepare the white ox of the open field, cook fragrant rice of millet, boil wild vegetable soup, and sing the village field music. Now, at this deep night and quiet hour, I share the winter with you all.

However, to pull oneself from poverty and make oneself wealthy is something rarely heard of in antiquity or today. To step upon this critical juncture is to transcend all things and go beyond the mundane world.
Here in my humble monastery, it is empty and vast, clear and distinct. Above, below, and in the four cardinal directions—east wall striking west wall;

in the center, there is not a single thing. What can be used as a standard or rule? Fortunately, the administrative office has prepared the ritual implements and fruit offerings. [The Master] descends from the seat.
In the Cloud Assembly Hall, everyone was chewing here and there. Suddenly, one bit upon something;

only then did he realize that at this place, green willows are fit for tethering horses, and every household’s gate leads straight to Chang’an. Although this is so, should a person without a mouth encounter you, with what would you receive them?
If you can see it here, you will cut off the tongues of a thousand sages and reveal your lifelong essence.
A brilliant radiance! If you have not yet realized the underlying cause, do not disdain this lack of flavor; once you are fully satiated, you can forget the hunger of ten thousand kalpas.
[He] strikes the meditation seat.

The Master ascends the hall to recite the *Sengxiao jing* (Scripture on the Extinction of the Sangha) and to express his gratitude to the Supervisor of the Monastery. He relates that for a long time Yaoshan had not ascended the seat.
The monastery director said, "The assembly longs for the Master’s instruction; we hope you will look upon us with compassion. Yaoshan said, "Strike the bell!

As soon as the sound of the bell vibrated, the assembly gathered like clouds. Yaoshan ascended the seat, remained there for a long while, then descended and returned to his quarters. Just as he was about to close the door—
The head of the monastery followed up by asking, "The Master promised to preach the Dharma for the assembly; why do you not utter a single word?

The Master said: "O virtuous practitioners of Chan! The old man of Yaoshan was cautious at the beginning and guarded against the end; even the Buddha-eye could hardly fathom him.
When the Abbot met him on a narrow path, he carelessly let the opportunity slip away, and to this day, beneath the ages, it remains a subject of people’s talk.
